name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -12 point partisan lean
Weber's large financial advantage: $922K on hand vs. Bartie's negative cash position
Incumbency advantage for Weber with no outside spending against him
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at just 3%
model.rationale: The district's -12 point Republican lean, Weber's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge over a Democratic challenger with essentially no resources make this a Safe R race. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Weber win.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or polling showing Bartie within single digits would warrant a downgrade to Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in a southeast Texas district that leans heavily Republican, about 12 points to the right of the country. He enters the general election with roughly $920,000 on hand after raising nearly $1 million, while Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised under $30,000 and reports negative cash. No outside groups are spending against Weber.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, which all point one direction: the partisan lean, incumbency, and a large money gap. Prediction markets give Bartie only about a 3% chance. The forecast expects Weber to win comfortably, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
